claims.text: The driver's own telemetry shows a hold of 20 seconds, not the five minutes POL-NS-01 requires. The longest qualifying run in EV-GPS-00607 is 3 fixes, from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10, inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius for this pickup — a continuous dwell of 20 seconds against the 300 second minimum for the zone class recorded in EV-TRIP-00607. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive and limb (c) fails on the driver's own data, so the cancellation fee is not chargeable under that clause at all.

Once limb (c) fails, POL-NS-06 fixes the consequence in arithmetic: 300 seconds required, 20 seconds measured, a shortfall of 280 seconds, so the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded to the rider in full — whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The fee actually in place is SGD 4.00 on the cancellation-fee line of EV-FARE-00607 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and that is the figure to be returned.

The driver cannot repair the 280 second shortfall by summing separate in-geofence intervals or by excusing the gap, because the only route to either is POL-NS-06(i), which requires a traffic_advisory covering this pickup road and this window. There is none: EV-ADVIS-00607-01 is MISSING, carries weight 0.0 and has no payload. The driver's chat message to the rider, 'car park entrance closed, cancel pls', is therefore uncorroborated by anything in the record, and the shortfall stands at 280 seconds.

The trip record contradicts the driver's account of having waited. EV-TRIP-00607 records wait_time_min of 0.6 — roughly 36 seconds — between the 08:21:52 arrival marker and the 08:22:30 cancellation, and the GPS dwell of 20 seconds agrees with it. This is not a driver who held the pickup for the statutory period and then gave up; it is a driver who reached the pin and cancelled inside the same minute.

The rider was at the pickup pin throughout. The rider track in EV-GPS-00607 carries 14 fixes running 08:20:40 to 08:22:37 — covering the entire 20 second driver dwell and the cancellation — all 14 qualifying, with a mean distance of 11.49 m and a minimum of 9.04 m from the pin, far inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE that POL-NS-04 sets. That satisfies limb (c) of POL-NS-04 and destroys the factual premise of the RIDER_NO_SHOW code under POL-NS-01(d): the driver's counterparty statement that he 'couldn't see anyone matching' is answered by the same driver's admission that a person tried to open his door. I do not need POL-NS-04 to carry the refund — POL-NS-06 is strict liability and does not turn on rider presence — but the presence fact removes any suggestion that the fee was earned by an absent rider.

No driver compensation is payable on this record. POL-NS-07 is expressly conditional on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and the dwell shortfall defeats that condition; POL-NS-06 states in terms that where cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The gross figure the driver might point to, SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00, never becomes payable.

The disposition follows POL-GEN-03: the rider is the filing party, the contested amount is SGD 4.00, and the present state is a charge (payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 in EV-FARE-00607). A ruling in the rider's favour therefore returns the whole of that SGD 4.00 as a full refund rather than restoring or preserving the charge.

claims.text: The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-07T08:21:52, which satisfies limb (a) of POL-NS-01: that limb asks only whether the trip_record contains an arrival event, and it does.

Arrival is independently established on the trace. The pickup is a LARGE_VENUE zone, so the arrival radius is 120 m under the fee schedule for that class, and the driver's GPS trace shows three consecutive qualifying in-radius fixes running from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10, the first of which precedes the 08:21:52 'arrived' event. POL-NS-02 therefore deems the driver arrived and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met.

The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) of POL-NS-01 recognises, and the trip record itself records no boarding event (started_at is null and the status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER). Limb (d) is met on the record.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Limb (b) of that clause requires that the driver neither replied in chat within 120 seconds of the rider's message nor placed any in-app voice call before terminating the trip. The trip record shows two in-app calls placed by the driver and answered by the rider (08:13:40 lasting 50 s and 08:17:40 lasting 30 s), both before the 08:22:30 cancellation, so limb (b) fails and the clause is unavailable whatever the chat contains.

Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 fails as well. The rider's only message, 'you cancel, not me' sent at 08:15:40, gives no position, entrance, block or bay identifier, requests no position and says nothing about not seeing the vehicle; it is neither locating nor coordinating, and the rider's only contribution was to refuse to cancel.

There is no false-arrival marker for POL-NS-05 to record against the driver. At the 08:21:52 arrival timestamp the trace is inside the geofence — its closest recorded fix is about 7 m from the pin, nowhere near the 300 m threshold — and the qualifying in-geofence run from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10 is a stationary hold, not motion at or above 15 km/h, so the waiting clock is not reset and no false-arrival referral is triggered.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties: this dispute concerns the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee charged on trip TRP-00607.

The fee can stand only if all four conditions in POL-NS-01 are met. Three are met. (a) The trip record EV-TRIP-00607 records a driver 'arrived' event at 08:21:52. (b) The GPS trace EV-GPS-00607 places the driver inside the arrival radius from 08:21:50 — at or before that event — with three consecutive qualifying in-radius fixes, and the radius for this pickup is 120 m because the trip record classes the pickup as LARGE_VENUE; under POL-NS-02 the driver is therefore deemed to have arrived. (d) The trip was terminated by the driver at 08:22:30 with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the codes limb (d) recognises, and no boarding was recorded.

The fourth condition fails. Limb (c) requires a continuous in-geofence dwell of at least 300 seconds for a LARGE_VENUE pickup, measured from the first qualifying in-geofence fix and not from the arrival tap. The driver's own telemetry shows a longest qualifying in-geofence run of 20 seconds — three fixes, 08:21:50 to 08:22:10 — and the trip record independently records wait_time_min 0.6, about 36 seconds, between the 08:21:52 marker and the 08:22:30 cancellation. Against the required 300 seconds that is a shortfall of 280 seconds.

Because limb (c) fails, the fee is not chargeable under POL-NS-01, and POL-NS-06 decides the consequence: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the zone-class minimum, the cancellation fee is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded to messages. The cancellation-fee line on the ledger EV-FARE-00607 is SGD 4.00 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00), and the whole SGD 4.00 is returned to the rider. No accumulation of separate intervals is available: the trace shows a single in-geofence interval, so POL-NS-06(i) has nothing to add.

Driver compensation is nil. POL-NS-07 pays the driver 80% of the fee only where POL-NS-01 is satisfied in full, and it is not; POL-NS-06 states expressly that no driver compensation is payable on a shortfall. The SGD 3.20 figure in the fare breakdown therefore never becomes payable, and no pin-ambiguity goodwill arises because POL-NS-03 is not engaged — the driver was at the pin, inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the venue.

The driver's arguments are accepted so far as they go, but none cures the shortfall: the arrival event; the in-radius fixes; the RIDER_NO_SHOW code; the two answered in-app calls, which do defeat POL-NS-04 (its limb (b) fails because the driver both called and was answered, and its limb (a) fails because 'you cancel, not me' is neither locating nor coordinating); and the absence of any false-arrival marker under POL-NS-05 (at the arrival timestamp the driver was about 7 m from the pin and stationary, not 300 m away or moving at 15 km/h). The rider's presence evidence — 14 rider fixes, mean 11.5 m from the pin, inside the 150 m presence radius — is accepted; it is not what carries the refund, because POL-NS-06 does not turn on presence, but it removes any suggestion that an absent rider earned the charge.

The driver's statement that he cancelled 'after waiting' is not borne out by the platform's own telemetry, which records a hold of 20 seconds. The rider's account that the vehicle drove off at speed and the door nearly struck him concerns driving conduct rather than the fee; no clause in this no-show policy produces a referral on it, so it is not decided here and is left for the rider to raise through the proper channel.

No escalation trigger applies. No artifact impaired under the integrity limbs carries the deciding fact — the GPS trace has 100% coverage, no sampling gaps and a 10-second cadence, and the trip record independently records the short wait; the profiles show no repeat no-show dispute between these parties and no anti-farming pattern (driver no_show_terminations_30d is 1 against 110 completed trips in 30 days); and no admissible artifacts contradict each other on the dwell.

Confidence is 0.95. The deciding fact is carried by EV-GPS-00607 and by EV-TRIP-00607, both at weight 1.0, so nothing discounts it.

ruling.explanation:
To the rider and the driver: the SGD 4.00 no-show cancellation fee is refunded to the rider in full.

The driver's arrival itself is not in doubt. The trip record carries an 'arrived' event at 08:21:52 (EV-TRIP-00607), and the GPS trace shows three consecutive qualifying fixes inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, the first at 08:21:50, i.e. before that event (EV-GPS-00607). So POL-NS-01 limbs (a) and (b), and POL-NS-02, are satisfied. The failure is the wait. POL-NS-01 limb (c) requires the driver to hold position inside the geofence for a continuous 300 seconds at a large venue (fee_schedule.minimum_dwell_sec). The longest qualifying run in EV-GPS-00607 is 20 seconds — 3 fixes from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10 — and the trip record's own wait_time_min of 0.6 (about 36 seconds between the 08:21:52 arrival marker and the 08:22:30 cancellation) agrees. That is a shortfall of 280 seconds.

POL-NS-06 makes the consequence arithmetic and strict: where the effective in-geofence dwell is shorter than the minimum for the zone class, the cancellation fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider answered messages. The fee in place on the cancellation-fee line of EV-FARE-00607 is SGD 4.00 (payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00, total_charged 4.00), and that is the sum returned.

On the driver's claims: it is accepted that the trip record contains an arrival event, that arrival is independently established on the trace, that the reason code is RIDER_NO_SHOW (one of the three limb (d) recognises), and that POL-NS-05 produces no false-arrival referral — at 08:21:52 the closest fix is about 7 m from the pin and the run is a stationary hold, nowhere near the 300 m or 15 km/h trigger. Those points are outweighed: a recognised cancellation code cannot stand in for the waiting period the fee is consideration for, and limb (d) itself requires termination at or after the required dwell elapsed, which it never did. It is also accepted, in the driver's favour, that POL-NS-04 does not rescue the rider — the rider's only message, 'you cancel, not me', is not a locating or coordinating message, and the driver placed two answered in-app calls before cancelling, so limbs (a) and (b) both fail. That does not change the outcome, because the refund rests on POL-NS-06, which does not depend on the rider.

On the rider's claims: the 20-second dwell against the 300-second minimum, the 280-second shortfall, and the 4.00 figure to be returned are all accepted and are the grounds of this ruling. The rider-tracking evidence (14 qualifying fixes, mean 11.49 m from the pin) is accepted, but it is not needed — POL-NS-06 is indifferent to rider presence — and with POL-NS-04 unavailable it decides nothing. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 is conditional on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and it is not, and POL-NS-06 says expressly that no compensation is payable where cumulative dwell falls short; the SGD 3.20 gross figure never becomes payable. The driver's statement that he 'cancelled as no-show after waiting' is evidence, but POL-NS-01(c) fixes the dwell by the trace, and the measured hold is what governs.

The missing traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00607-01, weight 0.0) has no effect on the outcome: it is material only to POL-NS-06(i), which permits separate in-geofence intervals to be summed, and the trace shows a single interval, so there is nothing to accumulate and no limb turns on it.

Confidence is 0.90. The deciding measurements — the 20-second dwell and the 0.6-minute wait — are carried by EV-GPS-00607 and EV-TRIP-00607, both at full weight 1.0, and no POL-NS-08 impairment applies (the trace has 100% coverage, no gaps, and 71 fixes; the chat log matches trip_record.chat_message_count). No escalation trigger under POL-NS-09 is met, and no clause produces a referral.

The driver's route to accumulate dwell across separate intervals under POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable and I do not apply it: it requires a traffic_advisory whose geometry covers this pickup road and whose window covers the waiting period, and EV-ADVIS-00607-01 is MISSING with weight_multiplier 0.0 and no payload, so the limb cannot be run (in any event EV-GPS-00607 shows the driver reaching 496 m from the pin, outside the clause's 300 m leash). The chat message 'car park entrance closed, cancel pls' is not a substitute for the advisory the clause names. No driver compensation is payable: POL-NS-07 is expressly conditional on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and POL-NS-06 states that where the cumulative dwell falls short, the full refund stands and no compensation is payable; the SGD 3.20 figure is the conditional 80 percent amount and never becomes payable. The POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip either — driver_profile.no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below the threshold of 4, and 1/110 = 0.009, below 0.08 — so no escalation arises on that ground. On the rider's side, POL-NS-04 does not carry this refund and I do not rely on it: limb (b) fails because the driver placed two in-app calls, both answered (08:13:40 for 50 s and 08:17:40 for 30 s), before the 08:22:30 termination, and limb (a) fails because 'you cancel, not me' is neither locating nor coordinating. Your presence at the pin is nonetheless supported — 14 qualifying rider fixes from 08:20:40 to 08:22:37 at a mean distance of 11.49 m, well inside the 150 m rider radius — and the driver's own counterparty statement that a person tried to open his door corroborates it; but the refund rests on POL-NS-06, which is strict liability and does not turn on rider presence. The driver's account of having looked and waited is answered by his own telemetry, which shows a 20 second hold and a cancellation inside the same minute. Confidence is 0.95. Both artifacts carrying the deciding fact — EV-GPS-00607 and EV-TRIP-00607 — are COMPLETE at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the POL-GEN-02(2) cap is 1.0, above the 0.70 floor; the only impaired artifact is EV-ADVIS-00607-01 (MISSING, weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), and nothing in this ruling rests on it — its absence is precisely what leaves the shortfall unrepaired. The counterparty statement carries no weight_multiplier and so enters neither the minimum nor the maximum of the cap; it is evidence, and it meets no limb here. No POL-NS-09 trigger fires: no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or presence and POL-NS-06 resolves the driver's account against the record; the anti-farming and cross-dispute counters are all below threshold (no_show_disputes_30d 0; disputes_with_counterparty_90d 0 and 0). The rider's account of the driver flooring the vehicle at the door is noted as an open question for the platform's driver-conduct review, but no clause in this category produces a referral for it.

ruling.amount_figures_used: cancellation_fee SGD 4.00 (EV-FARE-00607); required dwell 300 s (LARGE_VENUE, POL-NS-01/fee_schedule); measured dwell 20 s and shortfall 280 s (EV-GPS-00607); withheld driver compensation SGD 3.20 (POL-NS-07); confidence floor 0.70 (POL-NS-09).
ruling.explanation:
Rider — your dispute succeeds. Driver — the cancellation fee is refunded to the rider and no compensation is payable to you.

Why the charge cannot stand. POL-NS-01 is conjunctive: the driver side must carry all four limbs, and the fee is chargeable only if every one holds. Limb (a) is met (EV-TRIP-00607 carries a driver 'arrived' event at 08:21:52); limb (b) is met (EV-GPS-00607 shows three consecutive in-radius fixes from 08:21:50, inside the 120 m LARGE_VENUE arrival radius, the first preceding the arrival event, so POL-NS-02 deems arrival); limb (d) is met (the trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, a code limb (d) recognises, with no boarding event). Limb (c) fails on the driver's own telemetry: the pickup is a LARGE_VENUE zone (EV-TRIP-00607), so the required continuous in-geofence dwell is 300 seconds, but the longest qualifying run in EV-GPS-00607 is 3 fixes from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10 — a dwell of 20 seconds, measured from the first qualifying fix and not from the arrival marker, exactly as limb (c) directs. That is a shortfall of 280 seconds; the trip record's wait_time_min of 0.6 (about 36 s) is consistent. A conjunctive clause fails if any single limb fails.

POL-NS-06 then fixes the remedy in arithmetic, and it is strict liability: 300 seconds required, 20 seconds measured, and where the effective dwell is shorter than the minimum the fee is not chargeable and is refunded in full, whether or not the rider was present and whether or not the rider responded. The fee in issue is the cancellation-fee line of EV-FARE-00607 — SGD 4.00, payment_status CHARGED, refund_issued_sgd 0.00 — and the whole of it is returned. The accumulation route in POL-NS-06(i) is unavailable on this record: the traffic advisory EV-ADVIS-00607-01 is MISSING (weight 0.0, issue MISSING_ARTIFACT), so the driver's chat message that the car park entrance was closed is uncorroborated and neither extends nor excuses the shortfall.

The other candidate clauses do not displace the refund. POL-NS-03 does not apply: the driver was inside the arrival radius, not at a wrong face of the venue — the closest recorded fix was about 7 m from the pin, nowhere near the 400 m wrong-entrance test. POL-NS-05 does not apply: the arrival marker was legitimate (the driver was stationary inside the geofence, not more than 300 m out and not in motion at or above 15 km/h), so the waiting clock is not reset and no false-arrival referral is recorded. POL-NS-04 does not apply either — the rider's only message, 'you cancel, not me' at 08:15:40, gives no position, entrance, block or bay and requests none, so limb (a) is not satisfied, and the driver placed two answered in-app calls (08:13:40, 50 s; 08:17:40, 30 s) before the 08:22:30 cancellation, so limb (b) fails as well — but none of that matters to the money, because POL-NS-06 does not turn on rider presence or rider response.

The rider's presence point is accepted but not needed: EV-GPS-00607's rider track carries 14 qualifying fixes from 08:20:40 to 08:22:37 at a mean of 11.49 m from the pin, well inside the 150 m LARGE_VENUE rider-presence radius. It answers any suggestion that the fee was earned against an absent rider, but the refund already follows from the dwell shortfall alone.

Driver compensation is nil. POL-NS-07 is expressly conditional on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and it is not, and POL-NS-06 states in terms that where cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The SGD 3.20 that would have been payable on a verified no-show therefore never becomes due.

Confidence and escalation. The deciding fact — the 20-second dwell against the 300-second minimum — is carried by EV-GPS-00607 and EV-TRIP-00607, each at weight_multiplier 1.0, so the cap under POL-GEN-02(2) is 1.0 and my confidence is 0.9, above the 0.70 floor. None of the POL-NS-09 triggers fires: there is no impairment under POL-NS-08(a)–(d) (arrival-to-fix offset 2 s, well under 90 s; max_gap_sec 0.0 with 71 fixes and the rider track present; the chat holds 2 messages, matching trip_record.chat_message_count; and the SGD 4.00 cancellation fee equals the greater of the LARGE_VENUE zone-class fee and the RYDE_X vehicle-tier fee, SGD 4.00, so POL-NS-08(d) reconciles); no two admissible artifacts contradict each other on arrival, dwell or rider presence; the same-pair dispute counters are 0 and 0; and the POL-NS-07 anti-farming check does not trip (no_show_terminations_30d is 1, below 4, against 110 completed_trips_30d). No referral is produced by any clause.

For the human reviewer, an open question the money does not reach (not a referral): the rider's account that the vehicle moved off as the door was held, and the driver's account that he took the person at the door to be a different booking, are a conduct matter outside this category's remedies; nothing in the loaded policy directs a referral for it.

ledger.claim: The trip record contradicts the driver's account of having waited. EV-TRIP-00607 records wait_time_min of 0.6 — roughly 36 seconds — between the 08:21:52 arrival marker and the 08:22:30 cancellation, and the GPS dwell of 20 seconds agrees with it. This is not a driver who held the pickup for the statutory period and then gave up; it is a driver who reached the pin and cancelled inside the same minute.

The rider was at the pickup pin throughout. The rider track in EV-GPS-00607 carries 14 fixes running 08:20:40 to 08:22:37 — covering the entire 20 second driver dwell and the cancellation — all 14 qualifying, with a mean distance of 11.49 m and a minimum of 9.04 m from the pin, far inside the 150 m rider presence radius for LARGE_VENUE that POL-NS-04 sets. That satisfies limb (c) of POL-NS-04 and destroys the factual premise of the RIDER_NO_SHOW code under POL-NS-01(d): the driver's counterparty statement that he 'couldn't see anyone matching' is answered by the same driver's admission that a person tried to open his door. I do not need POL-NS-04 to carry the refund — POL-NS-06 is strict liability and does not turn on rider presence — but the presence fact removes any suggestion that the fee was earned by an absent rider.

No driver compensation is payable on this record. POL-NS-07 is expressly conditional on POL-NS-01 being satisfied in full, and the dwell shortfall defeats that condition; POL-NS-06 states in terms that where cumulative dwell falls short of the minimum the full refund stands and no driver compensation is payable. The gross figure the driver might point to, SGD 3.20 of the SGD 4.00, never becomes payable.

The disposition follows POL-GEN-03: the rider is the filing party, the contested amount is SGD 4.00, and the present state is a charge (payment_status CHARGED with refund_issued_sgd 0.00 in EV-FARE-00607). A ruling in the rider's favour therefore returns the whole of that SGD 4.00 as a full refund rather than restoring or preserving the charge.
The trip record carries a driver 'arrived' event at 2026-09-07T08:21:52, which satisfies limb (a) of POL-NS-01: that limb asks only whether the trip_record contains an arrival event, and it does.

Arrival is independently established on the trace. The pickup is a LARGE_VENUE zone, so the arrival radius is 120 m under the fee schedule for that class, and the driver's GPS trace shows three consecutive qualifying in-radius fixes running from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10, the first of which precedes the 08:21:52 'arrived' event. POL-NS-02 therefore deems the driver arrived and limb (b) of POL-NS-01 is met.

The trip was terminated by the driver with cancellation_reason_code RIDER_NO_SHOW, one of the three codes limb (d) of POL-NS-01 recognises, and the trip record itself records no boarding event (started_at is null and the status is CANCELLED_BY_DRIVER). Limb (d) is met on the record.

POL-NS-04 cannot exonerate the rider. Limb (b) of that clause requires that the driver neither replied in chat within 120 seconds of the rider's message nor placed any in-app voice call before terminating the trip. The trip record shows two in-app calls placed by the driver and answered by the rider (08:13:40 lasting 50 s and 08:17:40 lasting 30 s), both before the 08:22:30 cancellation, so limb (b) fails and the clause is unavailable whatever the chat contains.

Limb (a) of POL-NS-04 fails as well. The rider's only message, 'you cancel, not me' sent at 08:15:40, gives no position, entrance, block or bay identifier, requests no position and says nothing about not seeing the vehicle; it is neither locating nor coordinating, and the rider's only contribution was to refuse to cancel.

There is no false-arrival marker for POL-NS-05 to record against the driver. At the 08:21:52 arrival timestamp the trace is inside the geofence — its closest recorded fix is about 7 m from the pin, nowhere near the 300 m threshold — and the qualifying in-geofence run from 08:21:50 to 08:22:10 is a stationary hold, not motion at or above 15 km/h, so the waiting clock is not reset and no false-arrival referral is triggered.
